title: Planning, and plans that go stale
objective: Compare planning first with deciding step by step, and see why a plan must be checked against what really happens.

sources.title: Anthropic: Building effective agents (Dec 2024): agents use tools in a loop; stopping conditions such as a maximum number of iterations; "ground truth" from the environment at each step
Yao et al. (2022), ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

simplifies: The model here is a script with fixed rules, not a real AI: a real model's choices vary between runs, and it might give up, ask for help or retry differently. Real planners differ: some re-check after every step, some only on failure. Token counts are illustrative.

challenges.title: The stale plan
challenges.prompt: The agent plans first and follows the plan without checking. After it plans, someone else books Room A. Make sure the team is told the right room.

predict.prompt: Booking Room A fails, but the agent follows its plan without checking results. What does the team get?

options.explanation: Nothing told the plan about Room B.

options.text: No email: the agent notices the failure
options.explanation: This agent doesn't look at results while it follows the plan.

options.text: An email saying the meeting is in Room A, which nobody booked
options.explanation: Right. The plan went stale, and nothing checked the result.

challenges.hint: When a step fails, what should happen to the rest of the plan?
challenges.explain: Re-planning on failure throws away the stale plan and starts again from the facts: find a free room, book it, then email.

challenges.title: Right, in fewer turns
challenges.prompt: Re-planning works but takes 7 turns. Get the team told the right room in at most 4.
challenges.hint: Is a plan written up front helping in this task?
challenges.explain: Deciding each step from the latest result adapts at once, with no plan to throw away. Plans help with long tasks; they just need checking against what really happens.

quiz.prompt: What makes a plan go stale?

options.explanation: Length isn't the issue; outdated assumptions are.

options.text: The world changes after the plan is made, so a step's assumption is no longer true
options.explanation: Right. Here someone took Room A between planning and booking.
This plan was in its notes; it was simply out of date.

quiz.prompt: Why should an agent check each tool result, even when it has a plan?

options.text: Results are the ground truth: they show whether each step really worked
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's guide stresses getting ground truth from the environment at each step.
Checking is about catching failures, not length.
The tool works the same either way; checking is how the agent learns the outcome.
